# March On Film Festival

> > March On Film Festival celebrates civil rights history, social justice activism, and diverse storytelling through documentary and narrative films inspired by the March on Washington.

The festival showcases emerging filmmakers and students exploring themes of racial justice, LGBTQIA+ rights, immigration, nonviolence, and institutional transformation. Content includes documentary series on the civil rights movement, student competitions, and profiles of influential figures like John Lewis, Diahann Carroll, and Suzanne de Passe.

## Key Topics

- March on Washington
- Civil rights movement
- Social justice activism
- Documentary filmmaking
- Student filmmaker competitions
- Nonviolence strategy
- Diversity and inclusion
- LGBTQIA+ rights
- Immigration and diaspora
- Emerging filmmakers
- John Lewis
- Martin Luther King Jr.
- Institutional transformation
- Gun violence healing
- Reproductive rights

## Festival Programs & Events

- [Programs](https://marchonfest.org/programs): Film festival programs featuring civil rights & social justice content

## Featured Films - Documentary

- [Deciding Vote](https://marchonfest.org/film/deciding-vote): Documentary on George Michaels' abortion rights vote in New York State
- [#BlackAtSMU](https://marchonfest.org/film/blackatsmu): Student doc on Black students facing racism at Southern Methodist University
- [BLACK STRINGS](https://marchonfest.org/film/black-strings): Doc on Milwaukee's Black String Triage Ensemble healing gun violence trauma
- [Born to Stay](https://marchonfest.org/film/born-to-stay): Documentary on teen Elvia facing mother's deportation in Upstate New York
- [The Petition in Boots](https://marchonfest.org/film/the-petition-in-boots): Animated student documentary depicting March on Washington events

## Featured Films - Narrative

- [Home](https://marchonfest.org/film/home): Student narrative on Nigerian immigrants pursuing American Dream in Brooklyn
- [Mon Afrique](https://marchonfest.org/film/mon-afrique): Experimental student film exploring diaspora through African mask journey

## Civil Rights Documentary Series

- [Episode Five: The Strategy of Nonviolence](https://marchonfest.org/episode-five-the-strategy-of-nonviolence): Documentary episode on MLK's nonviolence strategy & Montgomery Bus Boycott

## Festival News & Highlights

- [March On boasts stellar queer content](https://marchonfest.org/march-on-washington-film-festival-boasts-stellar-queer-content): Festival spotlight on LGBTQIA+ filmmakers & queer civil rights content
- [Civil Rights History in 1950s-60s as Seen Through Variety](https://marchonfest.org/civil-rights-history-in-1950s-60s-as-seen-through-variety): 1960s civil rights media coverage featuring James Baldwin debate
- [Maven: The Magnificent Life of Suzanne de Passe](https://marchonfest.org/maven-the-magnificent-life-of-suzanne-de-passe): Interview with Motown producer Suzanne de Passe on entertainment industry

## Resources & Educational Content

- [How to Heal Oppression](https://marchonfest.org/resourc/how-to-heal-oppression): Social justice guide on healing oppression & institutional transformation
